does: Soaks dried seaweed in cold water until it swells and turns soft, silky and bright green, then squeezes out the water and cuts away any hard rib.

intro.what: This method softens dried seaweed in cold water before draining and trimming it.
intro.why: It teaches you to allow for swelling and stop soaking when the desired bite remains.

how: Put a small handful of dried seaweed in a large bowl, as it swells to many times its size.
Cover it with cold water and leave it until it is soft and glossy.
Lift it out, drain it and squeeze it lightly.
Cut away any hard rib and cut the rest into bite-sized pieces.

cues.text: The seaweed has opened out and turned a glossy dark green.
It is soft and slippery, with no hard, dry centre.

mistakes.mistake: Using too much, so that the bowl overflows with swollen seaweed.
Leaving it in the water for too long, so that it turns slimy and loses its bite.
mistakes.fix: Lift it out as soon as it is soft.

quiz.question: Why give dried seaweed plenty of room in the bowl?
choices: It expands considerably as it absorbs water.
It must be kept pressed against the bowl.
quiz.because: Water opens and expands the dried seaweed, so a small dry portion can occupy much more room.

quiz.question: What comes after soaking and draining in this method?
choices: Leave the hard rib attached to keep it chewy.
Squeeze lightly and cut away any hard rib.
Return it to the water until it breaks down.
quiz.because: Light squeezing removes excess water while trimming removes tough parts that soaking has not softened.

quiz.question: Which feel suggests the seaweed has softened?
choices: Soft outside with a brittle centre.
Slimy and losing all its bite.
Soft and slippery without a hard dry centre.
quiz.because: The dry centre should soften while the seaweed still retains some texture.

quiz.question: The seaweed became slimy and lost its bite. What would you change next time?
choices: Lift it out as soon as it softens.
Keep soaking until its colour fades.
Use a longer soak in more water.
quiz.because: Prolonged soaking can damage the desired texture; checking softness prevents unnecessary waiting.

variant_of.differs: Dried seaweed swells very fast and to many times its size in cold water, so it is soaked for a short while only, then squeezed, and any hard rib is cut away.
